full_name: Stochastic Mirror Descent for General Nonsmooth Convex Stochastic Optimization
source_reference: Lan, First-order and Stochastic Optimization Methods for Machine Learning, Springer 2020 (Theorem 4.1)

problem.description: Stochastic convex optimization over a bounded convex set

variable_space.math: X \subset \mathbb{R}^m \text{ nonempty bounded closed convex}; \; \xi \text{ random vector on } \Xi \subset \mathbb{R}^d; \; F : X \times \Xi \to \mathbb{R}

assumptions.name: Convexity
assumptions.math: F(\cdot, \xi) \text{ is convex on } X \text{ for every } \xi \in \Xi

assumptions.name: Assumption 1 (i.i.d. sampling)
assumptions.math: \text{It is possible to generate i.i.d. samples } \xi_1, \xi_2, \ldots \text{ of realizations of } \xi

assumptions.name: Assumption 2 (Stochastic first-order oracle)
assumptions.math: \forall x \in X, \; \xi \in \Xi, \text{ the SFO returns } G(x, \xi) \text{ such that } g(x) := \mathbb{E}[G(x, \xi)] \text{ is well defined}

assumptions.name: Distance generating function
assumptions.math: v : X \to \mathbb{R} \text{ is continuously differentiable and } 1\text{-strongly convex w.r.t. } \|\cdot\|: \; \langle x' - x, \nabla v(x') - \nabla v(x) \rangle \ge \|x' - x\|^2, \; \forall x', x \in X^o

steps.name: Stochastic mirror descent update
steps.math: x_{t+1} = \operatorname{argmin}_{x \in X} \left\{ \gamma_t \langle G_t, x \rangle + V(x_t, x) \right\}, \quad t = 1, 2, \ldots

parameters.name: \gamma_t
parameters.math: \gamma_t > 0 \text{ (variable step sizes; optimal constant choice: } \gamma_t = D_X / \sqrt{k(M^2 + \sigma^2)} \text{)}

parameters.name: V
parameters.math: V(x, z) = v(z) - [v(x) + \langle \nabla v(x), z - x \rangle] \text{ (Bregman divergence associated with } v\text{)}

proof.description: By convexity of f and g_t in partial f(x_t), decompose using delta_t = G_t - g_t
proof.math: \gamma_t [f(x_t) - f(x)] \le \gamma_t \langle g_t, x_t - x \rangle = \gamma_t \langle G_t, x_t - x \rangle - \gamma_t \langle \delta_t, x_t - x \rangle

proof.description: Split the G_t inner product at x_{t+1} and apply Lemma 3.4 (with g replaced by G_t) to bound the x_{t+1}-to-x term
proof.math: \gamma_t \langle G_t, x_t - x \rangle \le V(x_t, x) - V(x_{t+1}, x) + \gamma_t \langle G_t, x_t - x_{t+1} \rangle - V(x_t, x_{t+1})

proof.description: Bound the residual using Cauchy-Schwarz, strong convexity V(x_t, x_{t+1}) >= (1/2)||x_t - x_{t+1}||^2, and Young's inequality bt - at^2/2 <= b^2/(2a)
Apply variance decomposition ||G_t||^2_* = ||g_t + delta_t||^2_* <= 2(||g_t||^2_* + ||delta_t||^2_*) <= 2(M^2 + ||delta_t||^2_*), which absorbs the factor 1/2
proof.math: \gamma_t [f(x_t) - f(x)] \le V(x_t, x) - V(x_{t+1}, x) + \gamma_t^2 (M^2 + \|\delta_t\|_*^2) - \gamma_t \langle \delta_t, x_t - x \rangle

proof.description: Sum over t = s, ..., k. V-terms telescope. Apply Jensen via convexity: f(x_bar_s^k) <= (sum gamma_t)^{-1} sum gamma_t f(x_t)
proof.math: f(\bar{x}_s^k) - f^* \le \left( \sum_{t=s}^{k} \gamma_t \right)^{-1} \left[ V(x_s, x^*) - V(x_{k+1}, x^*) + \sum_{t=s}^{k} \gamma_t^2 (M^2 + \|\delta_t\|_*^2) - \sum_{t=s}^{k} \gamma_t \langle \delta_t, x_t - x^* \rangle \right]

proof.description: Take expectation: E[<delta_t, x_t - x>] = 0 (martingale: E[delta_t | xi_{[t-1]}] = 0, x_t is xi_{[t-1]}-measurable), E[||delta_t||^2_*] <= sigma^2, drop V(x_{k+1}, x*) >= 0

key_lemmas.name: Three-point lemma (Lemma 3.4)
key_lemmas.statement_math: \gamma_t \langle g(x_t), x_{t+1} - x \rangle + V(x_t, x_{t+1}) \le V(x_t, x) - V(x_{t+1}, x), \quad \forall x \in X
key_lemmas.role: Provides per-step descent bound relating the gradient inner product to telescoping Bregman divergence terms

proof.description: Write the first-order optimality condition of the prox-mapping (3.2.5)
proof.math: \langle \gamma_t g(x_t) + \nabla v(x_{t+1}) - \nabla v(x_t), x - x_{t+1} \rangle \ge 0, \quad \forall x \in X

proof.description: Verify the Bregman three-point identity (3.2.6) from the definition of V
proof.math: V(x_t, x) = V(x_t, x_{t+1}) + \langle \nabla v(x_{t+1}) - \nabla v(x_t), x - x_{t+1} \rangle + V(x_{t+1}, x), \quad \forall x \in X

proof.description: From step 1, isolate the gradient term; substitute step 2 to replace the inner product with Bregman terms; rearrange
proof.math: \gamma_t \langle g(x_t), x_{t+1} - x \rangle \le \langle \nabla v(x_{t+1}) - \nabla v(x_t), x - x_{t+1} \rangle = V(x_t, x) - V(x_t, x_{t+1}) - V(x_{t+1}, x)
